findings.title: func_p scalar-function builder handle leaks on the registration error path
findings.description: register_jit_udf creates the builder handle func_p = duckdb_create_scalar_function() (L125) and frees it only at L136-137 (numpy.array([func_p]).ctypes.data -> duckdb_destroy_scalar_function), which sits AFTER the guard `assert rc == ducklib.DuckDBSuccess` (L135). If duckdb_register_scalar_function (L134) returns DuckDBError, the assert raises and the destroy at L137 never executes, leaking the builder handle (the catalog did not take a copy because registration failed). The single DOUBLE logical type is already destroyed by this point (L131-132), so only func_p leaks. The create<->destroy pairing is thus correct only on the success path. This is the sole lifetime asymmetry in the function: type_buf and func_buf are each created fresh, used once for the boxed-pointer destroy idiom, and freed exactly once on the normal path (no double-free, no UAF). In this example registration cannot realistically fail, so the leak is latent; it is flagged because haversine.py is the de-facto reference pattern for JIT scalar-UDF registration (docs/reviews .../understanding/examples.md sec 1), and a downstream caller copying it into a long-lived connection that re-registers (e.g. a name collision returning DuckDBError) would leak one builder handle per failed attempt.
findings.impact: One leaked duckdb_scalar_function builder handle per failed duckdb_register_scalar_function call. Benign in the example (registration always succeeds); a real leak in copied code that handles a recoverable registration failure.
findings.recommendation: Destroy func_p before asserting, or wrap the register/assert in try/finally so duckdb_destroy_scalar_function(func_buf.ctypes.data) runs on both paths. Mirrors the existing correct discipline that frees the logical type unconditionally before register.

notes: Focus questions, resolved: (1) Destroying the DOUBLE logical type at L131-132 BEFORE register at L134 is SAFE and is NOT a use-after-free, nor a leak avoided. duckdb_scalar_function_add_parameter (L128-129) and duckdb_scalar_function_set_return_type (L130) copy the LogicalType BY VALUE into the function object (DuckDB C API contract: both do `*reinterpret_cast<LogicalType*>(type)` assignment), so dbl_p is dead data by register time; freeing it is required to avoid leaking it and register never touches it. The boxed-pointer destroy (numpy.array([dbl_p], intp).ctypes.data) passes &handle; DuckDB frees and NULLs the slot; dbl_p is not read after L132 -> no dangling use, no double-free (single create, single destroy, even though the one type is reused 4x add_parameter + 1x set_return_type). (2) func_p stays valid through register (it is the object being registered) and is destroyed afterward (L136-137) because the catalog holds its own copy -> correct. The only asymmetry is the success-path-only destroy reported as EX-hav-MEM-1. (3) carray OOB / null-pointer: NOT a defect. n = duckdb_data_chunk_get_size(chunk) (L89) is the live row count and is <= STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE (2048), and DuckDB FLATTENS a C scalar function's input chunk before invoking the callback (the canonical C-API scalar-function contract; the official duckdb.h example reads data[i] for all i). This matters specifically here because the SQL `hv_jit(lat, lon, 37.7749, -122.4194)` passes args 2 and 3 (lat2/lon2) as CONSTANT literals -- without flattening duckdb_vector_get_data on a constant vector would back a capacity-1 buffer and a_lat2[i]/a_lon2[i] for i>=1 (L107-109) would read OOB. Flattening expands them to n contiguous values, so all carray((n,)) reads (L99-103) and the a_out[i] writes (L113) are in-bounds; the integer count(*) cross-check assert_results_match(r_arrow, r_jit) (L171) would have caught the garbage otherwise. duckdb_vector_get_data returns non-null for a valid flat vector. (4) dtype width: every carray uses float64, matching the DOUBLE physical type (8 bytes); the four inputs and the output are all DOUBLE -> no reinterpret. _cast_int_to_void_p is a bare inttoptr to voidptr_t (numbox lowlevel.py:48-53) with no truncation on 64-bit; intp pointers from duckdb_vector_get_data are bridged correctly at each call site. (5) numpy buffer (.ctypes.data) lifetime: type_buf and func_buf are live local references through their single destroy call; the destroy reads &handle synchronously and returns, so no lifetime hazard. (6) meminfo/NRT: a scalar UDF holds NO structref/NRT state across the boundary (unlike irr.py), so there is no export/release pair to balance; the @cfunc trampoline _haversine_chunk_cb is a module global (L116-118) so its .address handed to set_function never dangles for the connection's life. NULL-input handling is absent (L105-113) but reads allocated flat-vector slots (not OOB) and the data is dense, so it is a correctness caveat (already filed as EX-hav-1, COR) not a memory-safety defect. No critical/high/medium MEM defects found.
